item.title: Idaho family sues after irrigation shutoff ruins crops on 1,000-acre farm
item.description: An Idaho family, whose farm thrives along the Snake River, has initiated legal action against the state regarding an emergency order that ceased their irrigation due to dwindling water levels. This abrupt halt has jeopardized their crops and could threaten their agricultural enterprise. They assert that their property rights were infringed upon without due process or fair compensation, highlighting a larger issue surrounding water rights management in the region.

item.title: Georgia man grew farm to 1,600 acres; $3.2bn pipeline now runs through his land
item.description: Donnie Peek, a landowner in Georgia, is challenging a natural gas pipeline rerouting that impacts his property. The pipeline's path was changed to avoid a utility executive's residence, which raises questions about favoritism. Southern Natural Gas initially planned to use an existing easement on Peek's land, but later deviated from that route. Peek has filed a legal challenge with federal regulators to revert to the original route.

item.title: Albany’s oldest house reopens after 13-year, $3m restoration
item.description: The Van Ostrande-Radliff House, a historical gem built in 1728, has finally emerged from decades of obscurity thanks to a meticulous restoration. Now the proud headquarters of the Historic Albany Foundation, this iconic building is committed to preserving Albany's rich architectural heritage. Visitors can explore engaging classroom spaces, a well-stocked research library, and even a parts warehouse, all while immersing themselves in the colonial history of Albany.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: How Jensen Huang's $30M to Stanford University helped open engineering centre
item.description: In 2010, Jensen Huang and Lori contributed to establish the Jen-Hsun Huang Engineering Center at Stanford University. The center was designed for collaboration among engineering, science, and medicine students and researchers. It features laboratories, workshops, and a library to support academic pursuits and innovation. Stanford’s administration emphasized the importance of interdisciplinary work in modern engineering education. This initiative reflects a commitment to advancing future innovations and research.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: Val Kilmer turned 5,328-acre New Mexico ranch into retreat, then sold most of it
item.description: In 2011, Val Kilmer’s scenic Pecos River ranch in New Mexico changed hands after years on the market. Initially listed at $33 million, the asking price dropped to $18.5 million. The ranch not only boasted abundant natural beauty and guest facilities but also held a storied connection with Hollywood. Eventually, it was acquired by Texas oil tycoon Benjamin A. Strickling III and his wife, concluding Kilmer's chapter with the property.

item.title: Travis Kelce’s $5.35M estate: Why is a $75,000 sewer dispute escalating?
item.description: Travis Kelce’s $5.35 million Ohio mansion has sparked a growing dispute with neighbors over plans for a six-foot fence and extensive landscaping. Residents have raised concerns about wildlife safety, security and potential damage to a century-old shared sewer pipe, with one neighbor citing a $75,000 repair estimate. Kelce’s construction team says it has made several compromises, but some landscaping proposals remain unresolved following recent planning board discussions.

item.title: Global warming could make Russia richer. It could also bring Nato closer to its doorstep
item.description: As the Arctic warms, Russia faces both opportunities and significant challenges regarding its environment and infrastructure. The Northern Sea Route is becoming a vital transit corridor, potentially boosting Russian exports to Asian markets. However, increased traffic raises risks associated with accidents and environmental harm. Despite potential economic benefits, Russia must contend with severe infrastructure damage from permafrost thaw.

item.description: Hope and Sherfane Rutherford turned the match on its head with a 120-run stand for the fourth wicket. Rutherford smashed 84 off 37 balls, while Hope remained unbeaten on 102 off 45 as the West Indies chased down India's 250-run target with nine balls to spare.

item.title: Match-winner on captaincy debut! Farhan leads Pak to stunning chase vs Sri Lanka
item.description: Sahibzada Farhan made a remarkable debut as captain, scoring 89 runs and guiding Pakistan to an impressive win over Sri Lanka, successfully chasing down 183. The aggressive pairing with Maaz Sadaqat shone through, sealing victory with seven balls left in the first T20I. Sri Lanka had set a competitive stage, thanks to Lahiru Udara's 91 runs. The anticipation builds for the upcoming matches scheduled in Rawalpindi.

item.description: In Tamil Nadu, it was still “Thalapathy” Vijay and his TVK brigade making their presence felt. In West Bengal and Assam, the BJP strengthened its position by winning with big margins. Puducherry, meanwhile, remained firmly with CM N Rangaswamy's ruling AINRC. Tamil Nadu and West Bengal went to bypolls in two assembly constituencies each, months after their assembly elections brought new parties to power in both states.

item.title: 149.5kmph thunderbolt! Mayank Yadav leaves West Indies reeling in chase
item.description: India scored their highest-ever T20I total against West Indies, reaching 249 runs in 20 overs. Mayank Yadav played a critical role by taking three wickets during the powerplay. His impressive bowling performance included a remarkable delivery clocked at 149.5kmph. West Indies struggled to respond and were left reeling early in their chase.

item.title: 'This govt will fall': Rahul's 'guarantee' to allies amid protests against CEC
item.description: Addressing INDIA bloc MPs at the Central Hall of Samvidhan Sadan, Gandhi said the issue went beyond Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and called for the termination of the current government. "There is a much deeper problem than Gyanesh Kumar and it requires termination of this current government," said Congress leader Rahul Gandhi.

item.title: California cyclist, 73, rides 3,200 miles and raises $740,000 to fight child hunger
item.description: Mark Strauss embarked on an incredible 3,200-mile cycling journey over 69 days to support the No Kid Hungry initiative, raising an impressive $740,000 toward a target of $1 million. Along the way, he connected with numerous supporters and gained insight into the pervasive issue of childhood hunger in America. His endeavor highlights the ongoing need for accessible food resources for children, as the campaign continues its vital fundraising efforts.

item.title: India smash highest T20I total vs WI as Samson, Iyer and Tilak go berserk in Ranchi
item.description: India showcased their batting prowess against the West Indies, amassing an unprecedented T20I total of 249 runs. The highlight of the match was Sanju Samson, who electrified the crowd with an explosive 82 runs from 41 balls. Significant input from Ishan Kishan and Shreyas Iyer, alongside Tilak Varma's not-out 44, fortified India's position.
item.dc:creator: HIJAM RAJU SINGH

item.title: Gauhati HC grants bail to singer Amritprava Mahanta in Zubeen Garg death case
item.description: The Gauhati High Court has granted bail to Amritprava Mahanta, marking the first instance of bail being awarded in the case related to Zubeen Garg's tragic death. Bail was set at Rs 50,000. Garg, a prominent figure, passed away in a scuba diving incident in Singapore in September 2025, just days before his scheduled performance. In the wake of this, Shyamkanu Mahanta, the organizer, has also faced arrest.

item.title: Railways lose appeal over Rs 1.45 lakh payout for stolen bag
item.description: Delhi state consumer commission upheld an order requiring Northern Railway to pay Rs 1.45 lakh to Ajoy Kumar. Kumar's luggage was stolen from a reserved train coach while traveling from Delhi to Patna. Railway officials failed to prevent unauthorized entry into the coach. The commission found negligence by railway staff contributed to the theft and delayed FIR registration.
